title: Automated Alarm System
tagline: An off-the-shelf home alarm rebuilt around a Raspberry Pi and a custom Pygame panel
summary: A budget 4-channel RFID home alarm system upgraded into a smarter security setup driven by a Raspberry Pi. The Pi reads the alarm panel's LED alert lights as voltages to work out which door is open and when the battery is low, and it controls the alarm's power cord and onboard beeper through relays. A first version used a simple LCD screen and a single mode button; a subsequent version further expanded the user interface and available features with a fully customized Pygame GUI offering mode selection, color-coded sensor status, configurable per-mode behavior, lifetime statistics, and email and SMS alerts.

hero.alt: Cover image for the Automated Alarm System project

sections.heading: Overview
body: This project upgrades a basic alarm system into a sophisticated security solution using a Raspberry Pi. The enhanced system features advanced alert capabilities, a customizable user experience, and improved functionality for monitoring and managing home security.

sections.heading: Project Story
body: The original alarm system was limited to indicating which door was open by lighting up corresponding LEDs. To enhance its capabilities, I developed a system that integrates a Raspberry Pi to monitor and respond to various events. The initial version involved soldering wires to the alert lights, connecting them to a Raspberry Pi, which measured voltages to detect open doors and low battery conditions through LED flash patterns. This system utilized a simple LCD screen to display modes and a button to switch between the modes.

The subsequent version further expanded the user interface and available features. A fully customized GUI was created using Pygame, offering complex, reusable, and configurable parameters to suit user needs.

sections.heading: Hardware Components
body: Alarm System: Utilized a budget-friendly 4-channel RFID alarm system from Amazon.
Integration: LED leads are connected to a Pi Hat on the Raspberry Pi, which reads voltages. The alarm system’s power cord and onboard beeper are routed through relays controlled by the Raspberry Pi.
Connectivity: The system connects to the home network via a router and is powered by a UPS, with an HDMI cable linking to the control panel.
Additional Sensors: Integrated a motion sensor for enhanced detection capabilities.

sections.heading: Main Screen Features
body: Top Buttons: Settings, mode selector (Auto Home, Home Day and Night, Away, Out), and Wi-Fi status indicator.
Bottom Status Bar: Displays the status of sensors with color-coded indicators: open (red), closed (green), errors (yellow), no power (black), and unknown (gray).

sections.heading: Settings Screen Enhancements
body: Master Sound Settings: Adjust sound alerts for various conditions.
Mode Behavior Configuration: Customize how each mode responds to detected events.
Lifetime Statistics: View detailed analytics on system performance and usage.
Notification Management: Configure email and SMS alert behavior.
